---
title: "Research"
---

I have seven years experience in electrochemical research with the last five specifically working on water electrolysis. I am most interested in anion exchange membrane (AEM) water electrolysers: an advanced water electrolysis technology that promises to significantly reduce the cost of green hydrogen production. My PhD focused on developing operando diagnostic techniques to better understand degradation in AEM systems.

## Research Themes

### Electrochemical Testing

Full cell device testing of performance and durability.

### Operando Diagnostics

Identifying the causes of degradation with operando imaging and electrochemical techniques.

### Method Development

Developing new experimental techniques to address electrochemical research questions.

### Bridging Academia & Industry

Collaborative research that moves from lab to application.

## Current Projects

### Involvement in EU Research Projects

- [HyPrAEM](https://hypraem-project.eu/): High-Pressure Anion Exchange Membrane electrolyzers for large-scale applications. [Cordis](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101192442)
- [ENDURION](https://www.endurion.eu/): Efficient and Durable Pressurised Anion Exchange Membrane Electrolyser with Novel Triple-Phase Boundary and Stack Designs. [Cordis](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101192485)
- [ANEMEL](https://anemel.eu/): Efficient hydrogen production from low-grade water sources using non-critical raw materials. [Cordis](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101071111)
- [ASTERISK](https://asteriskproject.eu/): Integrated process for seawater electrolysis using a PGM-free anion exchange membrane stack. [Cordis](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101192454)
